items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: The interviewee (Jerry Blumberg) does not mention Spivak. Spivak is mentioned by the Interviewer as 'the head of the department' who stopped a series of recordings. The interviewee's response ('Yeah, well, of course...') does not indicate any personal connection or knowledge of Spivak.

ctx.x: I don't know anything about it. I think he finished it, and it was supposed to have been pretty good, but I don't know about the publication.

I never did know what happened to him. I know one funny thing that happened one day, he wanted to get Bunks' reaction to Jelly Rolls' Library of Congress records. He'd gotten a few of them that Lomax or somebody had given him tests, which Lomax really wasn't supposed to give out. I gave some later to Charles Smith and I, too, and then Spivak, the head of the department, found out about it and stopped it right in the middle of the series, or after we had about two-thirds. But anyway, one day he brought those up to…
Yeah, well, of course, when I moved up to New York, I think the Stuyvesant engagement was over already. That ended about the 10th or so. Well, this was the second.
